card.title: PlayStation 4 BLOD (Blue Light Of Death) & APU/RAM/Flash Diagnostics

claims.statement: A 1-second BLOD (turns on then off instantly) indicates a bad APU, shorted capacitors near the APU, bad solder joints under the APU, or a bad power supply.
claims.evidence: Observed symptom correlation with APU rail shorts and power supply 12V generation failure.
claims.quote: 1 second then off Bad APU - Check capacitors near APU for shorts Bad solder joint under the APU - Reflow or reball the APU. Bad power supply – Check if +12Von is created by the power supply

claims.statement: A 6-second BLOD where the fan does not spin or stops spinning indicates a faulty southbridge.
claims.evidence: Fan behavior tied directly to southbridge initialization failure during boot.
claims.quote: 6 second BLOD it will pulsing blue light for 6 seconds or it will stay a solid blue light for indefinitely period When fan is not spinning then the southbridge is faulty or if it spins and then stops spinning

claims.statement: Corrupted NOR flash memory can cause BLOD and can be validated and rebuilt using the PS4 NOR Validator software after desoldering the chip.
claims.evidence: NOR integrity is critical for boot initialization and software validation confirms data corruption.
claims.quote: Corrupted NOR software. Desolder NOR chip, validate or rebuild the software using The PS4 NOR Validator software. The PS4 NOR Validator verifies the integrity of the NOR flash memory

procedure: Check capacitors near APU for shorts.
Disconnect hard drive to test if it forces safe mode.
Desolder NOR flash chip and validate integrity using PS4 NOR Validator software if software corruption is suspected.
card.caveats: Reflowing or reballing the APU should only be performed after verifying rail shorts and NOR integrity.
